newsitem.title: DUBAI: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Sept 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - United Arab Emirates - Sept 28.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the United Arab Emirates press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- World's foreign ministers join forces to criticise Israel over Israeli-Palestinian violence.
- UAE President Sheikh Zaid bin Sultan al-Nahayan, in United States for medical treatment, receives phone call from Saudi King Fahd wishing him good health.
- Syrian President Hafez al-Assad says his country had reached an agreement with former Israeli government about Israel's withdrawal from Golan Heights.
- Dubai's economy picked up in first half of year; number of building permits issued increased, as did number of visitors.
- Palestinian death toll rises to 62 as three people are shot in al-Aqsa mosque.
- European leaders make joint appeal to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat to meet immediately to calm violence in West Bank and Gaza.
- Requests by illegal foreign workers for out-passes have dropped, but rush to buy tickets out of country continues ahead of new labour law effective from October 1.
- Allocation of al-Khazna shares will begin on Saturday after initial flotation was more than 13 times oversubscribed, with 50,000 nationals paying 2.7 billion dirhams for shares.
- Netanyahu stays adamant despite continued bloodbath. Israelis storm al-Aqsa mosque in Jerusalem.
- Immigrants leaving UAE under government amnesty for illegal workers are making last-minute purchases before their return home, boosting Dubai business activity.
